rationale: B wins by a nose because it is more useful as a founder's decision document, especially in the questions and refusals. Its line "No current news signal was supplied, so none of these angles is anchored to a live story" is the adult in the room; A's "Angle C will survive the hardest scrutiny" is too confident when that same angle rests on the unproven headline "Faire absorbs all the default risk." Both sets need their lawyerly qualifiers put back in, but B better shows where the pitch will break before a reporter breaks it for you.
gaps_in_A: "Faire isn't using a credit bureau" is not in the supplied facts. Order-history underwriting does not prove credit bureaus, banks, or financing partners are absent.
"Faire absorbs all the default risk" overstates the record. The update says Faire underwrites and terms are undisclosed; it does not prove Faire bears all losses.
"Faire has 700,000 of them and says its data shows it" decorates a company claim. The facts say Faire says cash flow is the top barrier, not that methodology or data has been shown.
"Angle C will survive the hardest scrutiny" is bad confidence. That angle collapses unless Faire answers default rate, cost of capital, funding source, and day-61 enforcement.
gaps_in_B: "eat the credit risk itself" and "paying brands upfront out of its own pocket" are asserted before proof. Those may be true, but they are not in the update.
"instead of routing retailers to a bank or a BNPL provider" invents the displaced alternative. No bank, BNPL provider, or prior financing setup appears in the supplied facts.

"retailers aren't ordering less because they expect fewer customers" creates a demand contrast the facts do not support. Cash flow being the top ordering barrier does not prove demand is not a barrier.
"ahead of whatever buying season the brands are working toward" is a mushy fake peg. If no seasonal hook was supplied, don't smuggle one in with a shrug.
